q01.key_idea: Find how many points each beetle has, then join them in order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
steps: The beetle on the left has 1 point. The beetle on the right has 2. The top beetle has 3. The bottom left beetle has 4. The bottom right beetle has 5.
From 1 to 2, the line goes straight across the middle.
From 2 it goes up to the top beetle, 3. From 3 it goes all the way down to the bottom left beetle, 4.
From 4 the line goes straight across the bottom to 5. Only picture D has these 4 lines.

choice_feedback.A: In the star, the top beetle is joined to the bottom right beetle, but 3 and 5 are not next to each other.
choice_feedback.B: Here the left beetle is joined to the top beetle, but 1 and 3 are not next to each other.
choice_feedback.C: Here the bottom right beetle is joined to the right beetle, but 5 and 2 are not next to each other.
choice_feedback.E: Here the line starts by going from the left beetle up to the top beetle, but 1 must join 2 first.

q02.key_idea: Count all the kangaroos, then share them so both parks have the same number.
steps: The left park has 14 kangaroos. The right park has 4.
Together that is 14 + 4 = 18 kangaroos.
Half of 18 is 9, so each park needs 9 kangaroos.
The left park must go from 14 down to 9. 14 - 9 = 5 kangaroos move.

choice_feedback.A: After moving 4, the left park has 10 and the right park has 8. That is not the same.
choice_feedback.C: After moving 6, the left park has 8 and the right park has 10. That is not the same.
choice_feedback.D: After moving 8, the left park has 6 and the right park has 12. That is not the same.
choice_feedback.E: 9 is how many kangaroos each park should end up with, not how many move.

q03.key_idea: Add up all the dots, then see how many dots must fly away.
steps: The beetles have 5, 7, 5, 6 and 4 dots.
We want 20 dots. 27 - 20 = 7, so 7 dots must fly away.
The beetle with 7 dots flies away.

choice_feedback.A: If the beetle with 4 dots flies away, 23 dots are left.
choice_feedback.C: If a beetle with 5 dots flies away, 22 dots are left.
choice_feedback.D: If the beetle with 6 dots flies away, 21 dots are left.
choice_feedback.E: With no beetle gone there are 27 dots, not 20.

q04.key_idea: Draw the same three steps again, starting where the first drawing ends.
steps: The pattern is a tall step, then a middle step, then a small step.
The drawing ends at the bottom, so the new copy starts there with a tall step, 3 squares high and 3 squares wide.
Next comes a middle step, 2 squares high and 2 squares wide. Then a small step, 1 square high.
Point D sits right on the top right corner of the new middle step.

choice_feedback.A: Point A is inside the new tall step, below its top line.
choice_feedback.B: Point B is above the new middle step. Nothing is drawn that high there.
choice_feedback.C: Point C is inside the new middle step, below its top line.
choice_feedback.E: Point E is above the new small step, which is only 1 square high.

q05.key_idea: From above, a disc hides every smaller disc under it.
steps: Look from the top. First you see the top disc.
The second disc is wider, so its edge sticks out around the top disc. You see it.
The third and fourth discs are smaller than the second disc, so they are hidden under it.
The fifth disc is the widest of all, so you see its edge. The bottom disc is smaller than the fifth, so it is hidden.
You see 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 discs.

choice_feedback.A: The wider discs under the top disc stick out around it, so you see more than 1.
choice_feedback.B: You also see the widest disc, the fifth one from the top.
choice_feedback.D: The bottom disc is smaller than the disc on top of it, so it is hidden.
choice_feedback.E: The third and fourth discs are hidden under the wider second disc.

q06.key_idea: Turn both sheets the same way, then put all their lines and dots together.
steps: In every answer picture the first sheet is turned a quarter turn: its dot is at the top left, with one line going right and one line going down.
So turn the second sheet the same way. Its line that points right now points down. Its slanted line that points up and right now points down and right.
Put the sheets together. The middle dot has one line going straight down and one slanted line going down to the right.
Only picture D shows that, with no extra lines.

choice_feedback.A: The middle dot has a line going right, but it should have a slanted line going down to the right.
choice_feedback.B: There is an extra slanted line from the top left dot to the middle dot, and the line going down is missing.
choice_feedback.C: There is an extra slanted line from the top left dot to the middle dot. No sheet has that line.
choice_feedback.E: The line going straight down from the middle dot is missing.

review.note: Answer pictures show the sheets turned a quarter turn clockwise compared with the two sheets in the question; laid on top without turning, no picture matches. Blind solver also noted this. D is confirmed only under that turn, and step 1 tells the child to turn the sheets. Please check the figure.

q07.key_idea: Walk along each path like the dog and count the right turns and the left turns.
steps: On path E the dog walks across, then turns down. Facing the way he walks, that is a turn to his right.
Then he turns to walk across again: a left turn. Then down: a right turn. Then across: a left turn. Then down to the bone: a right turn.
That is 3 right turns and 2 left turns.

choice_feedback.A: Path A has 2 right turns and 3 left turns.
choice_feedback.B: Path B has 2 right turns and 3 left turns.
choice_feedback.C: Path C has 1 right turn and 4 left turns.
choice_feedback.D: Path D has 2 right turns and 4 left turns.

q08.key_idea: Look at the bumps and dents that each spot in the hole needs.
steps: The hole is 3 pieces long. At each end, a grey bump pokes into the hole, so each end piece needs a dent on its outside.
Piece A has 4 bumps and no dent, so A cannot go at an end.
Could A go in the middle? Then each end piece would need dents on 2 opposite sides. Only B looks like that, and there is just one B.
So C and D go at the ends with their dents facing out, and B goes in the middle. A is left over.

choice_feedback.B: B is needed in the middle. Its two dents hold the bumps of C and D.
choice_feedback.C: C fits at one end, with its dent facing out.
choice_feedback.D: D fits at the other end, with its dent facing out.
choice_feedback.E: C and D are both needed, one at each end.

q09.key_idea: Each knot uses up rope, so a piece with more knots is shorter.
steps: All 3 pieces start the same length.
So the piece with 1 knot must be the longest, and the piece with 3 knots must be the shortest.
In B, the rope with 1 knot is the longest, the rope with 2 knots is in the middle, and the rope with 3 knots is the shortest.

choice_feedback.A: The rope with 3 knots is longer than the rope with 2 knots.
choice_feedback.C: The rope with 3 knots is the longest one, but it should be the shortest.
choice_feedback.D: The rope with 2 knots is the shortest, but the rope with 3 knots should be shortest.
choice_feedback.E: The rope with 1 knot is the shortest, but it should be the longest.

q10.key_idea: Copy each hand with your own hands to see if it is a right hand or a left hand.
steps: Hold up your own right hand and left hand next to the picture.
For each hand, look if you see the palm or the back, and on which side the thumb is.
Turn your hands to copy the picture. If only your right hand can copy it, it is a right hand.
Count all the right hands.

choice_feedback.A: Copy each hand with your own hands and count the right hands again.
choice_feedback.B: Copy each hand with your own hands and count the right hands again.
choice_feedback.D: Copy each hand with your own hands and count the right hands again.
choice_feedback.E: Copy each hand with your own hands and count the right hands again.

review.note: Blind solver agreed (C) but with low confidence on blurry clipart. Writer could not confirm 5 right hands: the fist (top middle) shows curled fingertips with the thumb at the top right, which reads as a right palm and would give 6; palm/back of several hands is unclear. Steps and feedback are method-only.

q11.key_idea: Count the spots on one side, then double them for both sides.
steps: On the side we see, the toadstools have 4, 3, 5 and 3 spots.
The other side has 15 spots too. 15 + 15 = 30, so 30 dwarfs fit.
36 dwarfs come. 36 - 30 = 6 dwarfs get wet.

choice_feedback.A: If 2 got wet, 34 dwarfs would fit. Only 30 fit.
choice_feedback.B: If 3 got wet, 33 dwarfs would fit. Only 30 fit.
choice_feedback.C: If 4 got wet, 32 dwarfs would fit. Only 30 fit.
choice_feedback.D: If 5 got wet, 31 dwarfs would fit. Only 30 fit.

q12.key_idea: List every number between 10 and 25 that uses two different digits from 2, 0, 1 and 8.
steps: Numbers bigger than 10 and smaller than 25 start with 1 or 2.
Starting with 1: 12 and 18. 10 is not bigger than 10, and 11 uses the same digit twice.
Starting with 2: 20 and 21. 22 uses 2 twice, and 28 is too big.
That makes 12, 18, 20 and 21: 4 numbers.

choice_feedback.B: 10 does not count, because it is not bigger than 10.
choice_feedback.C: Numbers like 11 and 22 do not count, because their two digits are the same.
choice_feedback.D: 28 does not count, because it is not smaller than 25.
choice_feedback.E: Only 12, 18, 20 and 21 follow all the rules.

q13.key_idea: Do the cutting one step at a time and keep track of each colour.
steps: First cut: white and grey are cut. 3 white become 6. 2 grey become 4. The 2 black stay 2.
Second cut: grey and black are halved. 4 grey become 8. 2 black become 4. The 6 white stay 6.
Total: 6 + 8 + 4 = 18 pieces.

choice_feedback.A: After the first cut there are 12 pieces. The second cut adds 6 more, not 2.
choice_feedback.B: The second cut adds 6 pieces, not 4. Do not forget the grey pieces from the first cut.
choice_feedback.C: Count again: 6 white, 8 grey and 4 black pieces.
choice_feedback.E: The white pieces are not cut the second time, so they stay 6.

q14.key_idea: Follow the sticks lying across from left to right and see where they overlap.
steps: From left to right, the sticks lying across take turns: middle row, then top and bottom, then middle row again. That makes 5 places in a row.
Each place is 5 cm long. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 25 cm.
But each place overlaps the next one by the width of a standing stick, 1 cm. There are 4 overlaps.

choice_feedback.A: There are 4 overlaps of 1 cm, so take away 4 cm, not 5 cm.
choice_feedback.C: There are 4 overlaps of 1 cm, so take away 4 cm, not 3 cm.
choice_feedback.D: There are 4 overlaps of 1 cm, so take away 4 cm, not 2 cm.
choice_feedback.E: The sticks overlap, so the pattern is shorter than 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5.

q15.key_idea: Take away the road to Mary's house to find the two other parts of the road.
steps: Anna to Mary is 16 km. The last 9 km is from the crossing to Mary. So Anna to the crossing is 16 - 9 = 7 km.
Mary to John is 20 km. Again 9 km of that is from Mary to the crossing. So the crossing to John is 20 - 9 = 11 km.
Anna to John goes from Anna to the crossing, then to John: 7 + 11 = 18 km.

choice_feedback.A: 7 km is only the road from Anna to the crossing.
choice_feedback.B: 9 km is the road from the crossing to Mary, which Anna does not use.
choice_feedback.C: 11 km is only the road from the crossing to John.
choice_feedback.D: 16 km is the road from Anna to Mary, not to John.
